Figure 1. Aza-polycyclic natural products. (A) Known compounds derived from arginine and (B) new aza-polycyclic natural products identified

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Genome mining of the pno cluster leads to new guanidino-proline containing natural products. (A) The pno gene cluster in Aspergillus
pseudonomius. (B) Analysis of metabolites from A. nidulans expressing different combinations of pno genes by LC-MS. (C) Proposed biosynthetic
pathway of 5.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Genome mining of car BGC leads to new bicyclic spiro compounds. (A) The car and (B) esh BGCs from A. carlsbadensis and E. shearii,
respectively. (C) Analysis of metabolites from A. nidulans expressing different combinations of car biosynthetic enzymes by LC-MS. (D) In vitro
reaction of 250 μM 6 with 25 μM CarB overnight leads to 7 and 8. (E) Proposed biosynthetic pathway of 7 and 8.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Genome mining of the esh pathway leads to a new cage-like compound. (A) Analysis of metabolites from A. nidulans expressing different
combinations of esh biosynthetic enzymes by LC-MS. (B) In vitro reaction of 250 μM diketopiperazine 10 with different combinations of purified
enzymes in the pathway. Co-incubation of 10 with EshB, EshC and EshD resulted in the formation of the final product 14. (C) Proposed
biosynthetic steps from 10 to 14.
